lines.caption: This is a tour of the change for issue 23, which turns CI's proof on every pull request into four comments.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
First, a verify script describes each before and after pair: what it did between the shots, and what they prove.
Then the verify job numbers every shot, and turns each pair into one wide image.
It uploads the shots and the pair images, and writes the verify comment.
You read the summary first, then each comment, with nothing hidden behind a click.
Every job writes into its own comment. The four are created once, in a fixed order.
After writing its comment, each job refreshes the summary from the others.
And a summary job runs after all the others, to write it one last time.
Until now, all of the proof went into one comment, about twenty thousand pixels tall on pull request 20.
Each comment is found by a hidden marker, and carries a hidden status line that the summary is built from.
A test that passes with a pair but no description of it now fails.
A pair counts as one number, and the smoke test always comes last.
The key result is left out of the verify comment, with a pointer to the summary instead.
The summary says whether the pull request is ready, or which check failed first.
If two jobs create the comments at once, the oldest of each is kept, so the order holds.
An older run never overwrites the summary of a newer commit.
The summary job also covers a failed build, after which the verify job never runs.
The summary has the checks table, the key pair, and the table of all shots.
The code review now keeps every finding the pull request has had, closed ones included.
The verify comment has the results, then every other shot in number order.
And the explainer comment shows this page, or why it is missing.
Each pair gets a small table: the shot number, the action, what it proves, and both captions, then one image.
Every shot number is a link that jumps to that shot.
Most of the work is in two new scripts, one for the shots and one for the summary.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The pair images were built from the real screenshots of pull request 20.
The issue's mockup was never attached, so the comments follow the issue's text.
All twelve pair images came out nineteen twenty pixels wide, and looked right.
The summary and the comment order were checked against a fake GitHub.
The verify script itself, and posting to a real pull request, were not run here. CI does both.
A fresh agent reviewed the diff and found nine problems, one of them serious. All nine were fixed.
The serious one: keeping every finding whole would make the review comment too long for GitHub. It now shortens old ones.
A run that was cut short now still publishes its shots.
CI's own review then found fifteen more. All four medium ones, and six small ones, were fixed by hand.
The comment order and the shot links can only be checked on this pull request's first CI run.
Part 3. What comes later.
Next is this pull request's first CI run: read the four comments, and click the shot links.
Then the screenshot audit, which fills the summary's audit row.
And last, a re-run of pull request 20's feature, to compare with the old comment.
In short: CI's proof now reads in the order you decide, with every pair side by side.
